answered.sql: SELECT cp.position FROM Creative_Position cp JOIN Marketing_Agency_Creative_Positions map ON cp.id = map.position_id GROUP BY cp.position HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT map.agency_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Marketing_Agency)

candidates.meaning: Return the position for each agency by joining the tables on their respective IDs and position IDs.
candidates.sql: SELECT C.position FROM Marketing_Agency AS M JOIN Marketing_Agency_Creative_Positions AS MACP ON M.id = MACP.agency_id JOIN Creative_Position AS C ON MACP.position_id = C.id

candidates.meaning: List the creative positions associated with each marketing agency.
candidates.sql: SELECT m.name AS agency_name, c.position FROM Marketing_Agency m JOIN Marketing_Agency_Creative_Positions macp ON m.id = macp.agency_id JOIN Creative_Position c ON macp.position_id = c.id

candidates.meaning: Show the creative positions for each marketing agency, including all possible positions even if not assigned to an agency.
candidates.sql: SELECT m.name AS agency_name, c.position FROM Marketing_Agency m CROSS JOIN Creative_Position c
